Second, the in-Korea D-2-to-D-4-2 route is backed only by a secondary reproduction that may be from an older edition. I could not read the 2026 manual text for it because WebFetch could not reach any site and the search budget ran out. Also, `abroad: true` on a NONE move is redundant, and the new note must be written in all four languages.

d4#5.reason: D-4-3 has no 'gives'. The engine's factsAt() applies the 'gives' of every visa up to and including the one a step leaves from. Without it, two kinds of reader get wrong results. A school student who honestly answers 'Highest completed education: Below high school' (edu 0) is blocked from D-2-1/D-2-2 (needs edu:1), so D-4-3 shows nothing open. This is reproduced by visa-map-audit/tools/sim.mjs case F1: 'no' becomes 'yes' with the fix. A graduate who answers 'High school' cannot honestly tick the only Korea checkbox, which reads 'From a Korean university'. profileFacts() then sets koreanEdu = 0, which blocks the Korean-school routes D-10-1 {koreanEdu: 1, ageUnder: 25} and E-7-Y {koreanEdu: 1}. 'gives' is the only way the engine can learn about Korean schooling. Every step out of D-4-3 assumes the person finished Korean high school, so {edu: 1, koreanEdu: 1} is what the person has after completing D-4-3, as engine.md requires. One residual approximation is already present in the targets' needs: koreanEdu 1 cannot express 'all of elementary, middle and high school plus 7 years before 18'. The notes (d4#2) have to carry that.
d4#5.correctedFix: data/visamap.yaml D-4-3, after `age: [0, 19]`: add `gives: {edu: 1, koreanEdu: 1}`. No per-move needs are required.

none-rest#0.reason: The repo does gate F-2-T as [{edu:4,rank:3},{experience:5}], so a reader with no degree and 5 years' experience sees it OPEN. In the advanced-industry track, education and career are cumulative, and career-only needs 8 years, so that gate is too loose. The proposed fix is too strict. It drops the 4x-GNI relaxation that its own evidence cites (education OR career alone is enough), and it ignores the MSIT science track in force since June 2026 (any ONE of awards, papers, commercialisation or career). Because it sits on the visa, it would also apply to every in-Korea edge (E-7-T, F-2-7, E-1, E-3, E-7-1, D-10-T). The gate should be the union of what can actually qualify.

    - {edu: 5, experience: 5}    # doctorate + 5 years' research (research track / MSIT track)

The 2026 manual's general in-Korea change to F-3, as transcribed, applies only after entry and on humanitarian grounds (pregnancy, birth, child-raising, illness) for visa-free or short-term entrants, and requires a statement of reasons. The map already treats every short-term → family move (F-6-1, F-2-3) as `abroad: true`, and the review marked that correct. `abroadFor: notified` would show an ordinary in-Korea change to every non-notified tourist; it rests only on the 2022 Visa Navigator's D-2-family line, which I could not check against 2026 text. For lawful long-term residents (D-2, D-4, F-1), plain in-Korea edges are right, and F-3's own needs gate them. Simulation: D-2-2 → F-3 is OPEN for spouse=foreigner and BLOCKED for spouse=none.

The path is not dead either: G-1-5 is in the current-visa search list, so a reader who already holds it can start there and reach F-2-4 → F-5-27. This matches round-2 visit#7, which made the same call.

A simulation shows that a high-school-only reader with 5 years' experience gets F-2-T as OPEN from E-7-1, E-7-T and D-10-T, because `[{edu:4,rank:3},{experience:5}]` means either one is enough. The base Top-Tier criteria are indeed degree AND career. But according to 고시 제2026-160호 as read by f2#6 and none-rest#0 (not re-fetched by me), an income of 4× GNI waives either the degree or the career condition. F-2-T also has a science-and-technology track (visadocs Ⅱ. 과학기술 분야), while E-7-T's needs come only from the industry track. The conjunctions are still the best gate the engine can express, since it has no income fact and PI-level science applicants are nearly always covered by {edu:5, rank:3, experience:5}. The 4× waiver should go in `how` so a blocked reader can see the exception.

e7-main#3.reason: The legal core holds: 별표 1의3 제8호 has a licence branch ('또는 법무부장관이 정하는 기술자격증'), needs only 3 years' residence in Korea, and names no prior status. E-7-4 and E-7-4R lack the edge, and F-5-10's visa-level needs `[{edu:3,stem:true},{koreanEdu:4}]` would hide a licence holder, so `needs: {}` on the move is the only way to express it. But the claim that E-7-4 points-table licences make holders 'the normal case' is not shown. The points table rewards 기능사/산업기사/기사, and which level the MOJ-listed licence must be is unconfirmed; the repo itself says 'engineer licence'. The route also needs a wage of 1× GNI (about ₩52.4M) against E-7-4's ₩26M floor, so the note should name the MOJ list, full-time work and the wage rather than imply any licence suffices.

e7-main#5.reason: The level-4 rule comes from the 2025-02-20 MOJ plan and is out of date. 법무부고시 제2026-248호 (amended, in force since 2026-08-03) put the F-2-R requirement back to KIIP 3 or TOPIK 3. Its 제4조제1항 was read in full by an earlier agent: 'KIIP stage 3+ (incl. pre-test placement 4+) or TOPIK 3+'. The repo's transcription of the 2026.9.18 sojourn manual's F-2-R change list agrees: '기본소양 요건 입증서류' = KIIP level-3 completion or pre-test placement at level 4+, or TOPIK 3+. The repo's `lang: {topik: 3, kiip: 3}` and 'KIIP 3 or TOPIK 3' are therefore correct for 2026, and the finding's practitioner blogs reflect the superseded 2025 rule.

The decree's F-5-6 ground is time on the 재외동포(F-4) status, and F-4-R is a sub-code of that status: visadocs records F-4>F-4-R and F-4-R>F-4 as within-status changes, and the F-4-R change uses the F-4 integrated application form. The fix is expressible. F-4-R>F-4 has a within rule (use: change), F-5-6 has a change list, and F-5-6's `stay: {years: 2, in: [F-4]}` already counts F-4-R years because isStatus treats F-4-R as F-4. Simulation shows F-5-6R, F-5-6 and F-4 all open from F-4-R. Caveat: no text names F-4-R in the F-5-6 rule, so 'F-4-R years count' rests on the status definition.

f-family#5.reason: Right that F-1 offers no F-2-99 while F-3 does, and that 방문동거(F-1) is on the F-2-99 eligible-status list (the repo's statusGroups.longTerm includes F-1 too). Wrong that the rule counts 'any long-term status other than A-1 to A-3': the manual narrows the decree to a closed list without F-3. So the consistent fix is the finding's alternative, dropping F-3 -> F-2-99. A lead that restates the manual limits the F-1 route to Korea-born Taiwanese Chinese (화교), and F-2-99 requires current economic activity, which F-1 rarely allows. The repo's KIIP exemption for Korea-born Taiwanese Chinese also fits this. A broad F-1 -> F-2-99 edge with the proposed generic note would therefore mislead most F-1 holders; if added, it should be gated to TW.

f-family#6.reason: True that nothing leads to F-1 and F-6-1 has no F-1 move. The 2026.9.18 manual documents '가사정리(F-1-6) 체류기간 연장허가' inside the F-6 chapter (and in the F-1 chapter), and the Visa Navigator says a 혼인단절 spouse who does not qualify as F-6 may change to F-1. Three corrections. (1) F-1 has only an `extend` list, so an in-Korea F-6-1 -> F-1 edge fails the test 'a move inside Korea goes to a visa the manual lets you change to there' unless a rule is added. It also shows no list on the docs page, whose makeMove honours `within` rules only for same-status moves. (2) The edge must be gated `spouse: exKorean` like F-6-3, or still-married readers see it. (3) The F-6-3 -> F-1 edge is unsupported, since F-1-6 is for those who do NOT qualify for F-6-3. Minor: the claim that F-6-3 is always blocked is wrong; it is open for an 'ex-Korean spouse' reader.

f-family#7.reason: Correct: F-4 how.en says 'former Korean citizen or descendant'. The decree defines 외국국적동포 by nationality held BY BIRTH, which the repo's manual-derived visadocs also uses ('Former Korean national by birth ... (F-4-41)'). However, the proposed text drops the decree's parenthetical that includes Koreans who emigrated before the 1948 government. Those are exactly the Koryo-saram who make up much of this site's Uzbek and Russian audience, and the new wording 'held Korean nationality by birth' could make them think they do not qualify. Keep that group explicit. The military-service sentence is right and should stay.
